entries.title: The Run
body: Explore rooms, survive fights, claim rewards, and push deeper toward the next boss.
Held embers travel with the run until banked, spent, recovered, or lost.

entries.title: Map and Rooms
body: Revealed exits show where you can travel next. Cleared rooms stay available as routes.
Combat, campfire, merchant, treasure, relic, and boss rooms each change the next choice.

entries.title: Character and Loadout
body: Equipment, attuned magic, item slots, relics, and progression stats shape your deck.
Most loadout changes happen outside combat, including pre-battle and campfire moments.

entries.title: Rewards
body: After combat, choose a card, take healing, or claim other room rewards when offered.
New magic cards enter reserve first; attune them from the character sheet to add them to the active deck.

entries.title: Relics
body: Relics are passive run modifiers. Some trigger in combat, some change card values, and some alter rewards.
Hover relic badges in the top HUD for their current text.

entries.title: Combat Board
body: Cards resolve against board coordinates. A target is legal only when the card's targeting rule, range, line of sight, occupancy, and terrain checks all pass.
Card previews show legal targets, affected tiles, and projected result values before resolution.

entries.title: Turn Clock
body: Each played card adds its printed time to the acting unit's turn delay.
The turn clock orders actors by current delay and previews the next activations.

entries.title: Card Plays
body: Each player turn begins with a finite card play capacity. Playing a card spends one play unless an effect states otherwise.
Card play effects add temporary capacity that expires at the end of the current player turn.

entries.title: Health and Defenses
body: Non-piercing damage is applied to block first, then stoneskin, then health.
Block resets on that unit's turn boundary. Stoneskin persists until damage or sunder removes it.

entries.title: Targeting
body: Melee actions target adjacent or pattern-defined nearby tiles. Ranged actions require a legal range and line-of-sight path.
Area actions resolve over a tile pattern. Push and pull resolve forced movement along a legal direction until distance, blockers, or terrain stop the target.

entries.title: Fatigue
body: When a draw request empties the draw pile, the discard pile reshuffles into a new draw pile.
Each reshuffle increments fatigue. Fatigue deals direct health loss that bypasses block.

entries.title: Traps
body: Traps resolve when the player enters their tile.
Trap payloads can apply damage, burn, poison, freeze, shock, or immobilize according to the trap definition.

entries.title: Elemental Intensity
body: Elemental intensity is a room-scoped value keyed by element.
Cards can require, add, spend, or scale from the room's current intensity according to their printed fields.

entries.title: Lightning Strikes
body: Lightning strikes select a set of target tiles from the action definition and resolve shock damage on those tiles.
Strike tiles are previewed before the enemy activation resolves.

entries.title: Summons
body: Summon actions create additional enemy units of the configured minion type.
Summoned units enter the normal turn clock, occupy board tiles, and use their own intent definitions.

entries.title: The Umbra
body: The Umbra hides board tiles beyond your current vision. Enemies concealed within it cannot be directly targeted, and their identities, intents, and threat previews remain hidden.
Umbra stages grow more severe deeper in the labyrinth. Radiance effects create light, extend your vision, reveal hidden enemies, or reduce the room's Umbra stage.

entries.title: Melee
body: Melee actions use short-range target rules, usually adjacent to the acting unit.

entries.title: Ranged
body: Ranged actions target distant tiles that pass the action's range and line-of-sight checks.

entries.title: Area Attack
body: Area actions resolve over every legal target tile in their configured pattern.
Some area patterns can rotate around the origin before the action is committed.

entries.title: Move
body: Move actions walk through reachable passable tiles.
Occupancy, terrain, movement range, and trap tiles are evaluated during path preview and resolution.

entries.title: Blink
body: Blink relocates the unit directly to a legal destination tile without tracing an intervening path.

entries.title: Block
body: Block absorbs non-piercing damage before stoneskin and health.
Block is cleared when that unit begins its next activation.

entries.title: Stoneskin
body: Stoneskin absorbs non-piercing damage after block and before health.
Stoneskin persists across turns until damage or sunder removes it.

entries.title: Heal
body: Heal increases health up to maximum health.
Card persistence after a heal is determined by the card's exhaust or consume fields.

entries.title: Draw
body: Draw moves cards from draw pile to hand up to the requested amount and hand-size limit.

entries.title: Card Play
body: Card play effects increase current-turn card play capacity by the printed amount.

entries.title: Flurry
body: Flurry snapshots every card play available when the card begins.
It repeats the card's printed actions and health cost once per play spent, but pays the card's Time only once. Card plays gained during resolution remain available afterward.

entries.title: Illusion
body: Illusion actions create allied decoy units with health.
Enemy targeting can choose illusions, and damage can destroy them.

entries.title: Immobilize
body: Immobilize prevents move and blink actions on the affected unit's next activation.
The immobilize flag clears after that activation is processed.

entries.title: Exhaust
body: Exhaust moves the played card to the burned pile instead of discard.
Burned cards do not return to draw or discard for the rest of the combat.

entries.title: Health Cost
body: Health cost is paid when the card is committed.
Health-cost loss bypasses block and stoneskin.

entries.title: Pierce
body: Pierce damage bypasses block and stoneskin.
Bypassed defenses are not reduced by the pierced damage.

entries.title: Bleed
body: Bleed stores a damage value on the affected unit.
Before that unit resolves a real move or attack action, bleed deals its stored damage. The bleed value clears after that unit's next activation.

entries.title: Burn
body: Burn deals its current value as damage at the start of the affected unit's activation.
After the tick, burn is reduced by the status decay value.

entries.title: Poison
body: Poison stores delayed damage and a countdown.
When the countdown reaches zero during turn setup, poison deals its stored damage and clears that stored damage.

entries.title: Freeze
body: Freeze skips the affected unit's next activation.
Freeze also doubles incoming damage while its stored value is above zero.

entries.title: Shock
body: Shock disrupts the affected unit's next non-movement action.
The shock value decrements during that unit's turn setup.

entries.title: Expose
body: Expose adds its stored value to the next damage hit against the affected unit.
Expose clears after being consumed by a hit.

entries.title: Sunder
body: Sunder removes block first, then stoneskin, up to the printed sunder value.
Sunder resolves before the damage portion of the action.

entries.title: Chain
body: Chain applies additional hits to eligible nearby enemies after the primary target is hit.
The printed chain value controls how many extra jumps can occur.

entries.title: Push
body: Push moves the target away from the action source up to the printed distance.
Forced movement stops when the target reaches an invalid tile, blocker, or maximum distance.

entries.title: Pull
body: Pull moves the target toward the action source up to the printed distance.
Forced movement stops when the target reaches an invalid tile, blocker, or maximum distance.

entries.title: Consume
body: Consume removes the played item card from the run after resolution.

entries.title: Radiance
body: Radiance cards carry light into the Umbra. Their effects include Illuminate, Vision, Truesight, and Dispel Umbra.
Radiance cards still follow their printed element, targeting, time, and card-play rules.

entries.title: Illuminate
body: Illuminate places a light source on the targeted tile and reveals Umbra within its printed radius.
Its counter shows how many player activations remain. A lasting light displays an infinity symbol instead.

entries.title: Vision
body: Vision temporarily increases the radius of light centered on the player by the printed amount.
The bonus counts down on player activations; when it ends, the Umbra gradually closes over newly hidden tiles.

entries.title: Truesight
body: Truesight reveals enemies through the Umbra and permits direct attacks against them even while their tiles remain dark.
Its player-HUD counter shows how many player activations remain. Truesight does not illuminate board tiles.

entries.title: Dispel Umbra
body: Dispel Umbra reduces the room's effective Umbra stage by the printed number of steps for the rest of combat.
It cannot reduce the effective stage below Clear.

entries.title: Tunnel Crawler
body: Fast close-range predator that closes distance and opens bleed wounds.
Its intents favor short movement paths followed by melee bleed attacks.

entries.title: Ash Acolyte
body: Ranged caster with ash bolt attacks, self-defense actions, and health-draining effects.
Its intents alternate between line-of-sight damage and preservation.

entries.title: Bone Harrier
body: Mobile ranged skirmisher with pierce and bleed attacks.
Its intents often combine repositioning with a ranged strike.

entries.title: Ash Warden
body: Durable front-line guard with heavy melee attacks, block gains, and close area strikes.
It can absorb damage through defenses before its health is exposed.

entries.title: Cinder Ooze
body: Fire-locked ooze that can split into droplets when killed.
Its death effect can add smaller cinder enemies to nearby valid tiles.

entries.title: Cinder Droplet
body: Small ooze fragment spawned by larger cinder oozes.
Droplets have lower health than the parent ooze and still occupy board tiles.

entries.title: Bile Bloomer
body: Earth-locked controller that applies poison and expose.
Its intents emphasize delayed damage and vulnerability setup.

entries.title: Chainbound Gaoler
body: Air-locked jailer that pulls, pushes, and restricts movement.
Its intents use forced movement and immobilize to alter reachable tiles.

entries.title: Grave Surgeon
body: Support enemy that heals or guards injured allies.
Its intents restore allied health or add block to allied units.

entries.title: Frostglass Lancer
body: Ice-locked striker that threatens freeze and long reach.
Its intents combine line-based reach with freeze application.

entries.title: Zekarion, the Raging Tempest
body: Boss creature that commands storms, summons wisps, and resolves broad area attacks.
Its intents include lightning strike patterns and summon actions.

entries.title: Lightning Wisp
body: Summoned lightning minion with shock attacks.
Wisps have low health and enter the normal enemy turn sequence.

entries.title: Worldspines
body: Tharokh raises attackable stone spires at fixed arena positions.
Faultline ruptures every tile near a surviving Worldspine, then breaks the spires. Destroy them early to carve safe ground.

entries.title: Cinder Marks
body: Vyraketh brands open tiles with cinder marks that can be attacked and triggered like traps.
On its next activation, Crownfire detonates every mark that remains. Each blast can overlap adjacent marks.

entries.title: The Hollow Gale
body: Vaeloryx's Hollow Gale reaches across the entire arena.
It damages the player, then pushes them away from the dragon one tile at a time; hazards encountered along the route still trigger.

entries.title: Crystal Armor
body: Iskaldra forms multiple layers of crystal armor.
Each damaging hit breaks exactly one layer instead of dealing damage, rewarding flurries and inexpensive multi-hit attacks before a heavy strike.

entries.title: The Last Eclipse
body: Noctyrax temporarily forces the arena to Eclipse and immediately harms actors standing without Radiance.
Placed light protects every tile in its radius. Personal vision, truesight, and Umbra dispelling protect the player when the Eclipse falls.

entries.title: Tharokh, the Worldspine
body: Earth dragon boss whose raised Worldspines reshape the arena.
Its Faultline intent turns every surviving spire into a local blast center.

entries.title: Vyraketh, the Cinder Crown
body: Fire dragon boss that covers the arena in cinder marks.
Crownfire always follows a successful Kindle Ground, creating a one-activation disarm window.

entries.title: Vaeloryx, the Hollow Gale
body: Air dragon boss that weaponizes forced movement.
Its opening gale sweeps the full arena and can drive the player through hazards.

entries.title: Iskaldra, the Rime Tyrant
body: Ice dragon boss protected by hit-counted crystal armor.
Break every layer with separate hits before committing high-damage attacks.

entries.title: Noctyrax, the Last Eclipse
body: Shadow dragon and final boss of the twenty-fourth depth.
Its Last Eclipse punishes unlit positions; preserved Radiance creates the intended counterplay.
